absent: Implementations behind shared helpers such as allowable-orders, split workers, huge directory splitters, and hugetlb zap helpers.
Valid order domain, huge size encodings, allocation and zone flag values, and sysfs order-mask management.
Lifetime, allocation, reference counting, and concurrency for huge zero folio and frame references.
Full state machines for collapse, split, migration, NUMA handling, userfault handling, and hugetlb reservation regions.
Lock ordering, acquisition contexts, and interrupt rules beyond which member guards which structure.
Error codes, fault codes, and recovery behavior for split, madvise, copy, move, and atomic-fill paths.
Address-space layout, page-table formats, and architecture-specific huge-entry predicates.

findings.text: Global transparent huge page mode is exposed through small queries over a flags word, distinguishing an always mode from an enabled mode that also accepts advised requests, plus a hardware disable query and a zero-page-use query.
A mapping counts as anonymous exactly when it carries no file operations hook; this classification selects anonymous-only order masking and skips file offset alignment checks.

A single candidate order fits a mapping only when file-backed offset alignment agrees with the candidate size and the aligned block lies wholly inside the mapping; anonymous mappings omit the offset test and a disabled build never reports fit.

Filtering a mask of candidate orders examines larger candidates first, prunes failures, and halts at the first passing candidate under the rule that smaller candidates then necessarily pass; a disabled build yields an empty mask.

A shmem huge allocation mask preserves caller zones while combining allow and deny allocation properties with a limit mask through intersection and union semantics; a disabled build returns the input mask unchanged.

Allowable orders for anonymous mappings outside forced collapse are narrowed by enabled-order masks chosen from advice state and global mode, returning empty when narrowed to nothing before deferring to a shared helper; a disabled build always returns empty.

Huge pages are refused under a per-mapping opt-out or a process-wide complete opt-out; explicit advice or forced collapse can permit use except under complete opt-out, otherwise a process-wide except-advised flag supplies the default.

Splitting is offered in list and non-list forms toward a target order, with conveniences toward base order and folio granularity that forward to a shared list worker; disabled builds warn once and report failure.

A populated middle or upper directory entry counts as huge per its architecture predicate, while a non-empty unpopulated entry is conservatively treated as huge and empty entries are not huge; disabled builds never report huge and generic predicates report false.
Conditional directory-split helpers recheck huge state at use time and act only when huge, otherwise having no effect; disabled builds define them as empty statements.
The transparent-huge spinlock for a middle or upper entry is only returned when the entry currently tests huge, otherwise null is returned; disabled builds always return null.
Middle-directory mappability holds when folio order reaches the middle-directory huge threshold, and an order matches that level on exact equality; disabled builds never report mappable.

Huge zero identity is tested against stored folio and frame references with block alignment, and directory entries by presence plus frame test; accessors expose a persistent huge zero folio when configured and otherwise fall back to the ordinary zero page, with disabled builds reporting false or null.
A transparent-huge size descriptor associates a kernel object with list linkage and an integer order, retrievable from its embedded object.

A huge subpool tracks counts, limits, minima, reservations, and its backing state; a reservation map tracks references, regions, cache accounting, and optional cgroup charging; a reserved interval tracks bounds; a VMA lock object binds references and a semaphore to a mapping.

Subpool and reservation mutation use embedded spinlocks, region stability uses a read-write semaphore, hugetlb VMA membership uses its own semaphore, and process flag queries use an atomic bit test on private flags.

Huge table helpers locate an entry from directory plus address via page address and index, allocate backing tables on demand, iterate configured huge states, and gate zap begin and end work to hugetlb mappings.

Page and folio warn-once diagnostics evaluate once, emit detailed state and warn only on first true evaluation per site, and yield the outcome; non-debug builds reduce them to a condition validity check.
The used-subpage count constant has value three.
The split-type enumeration defines uniform and non-uniform kinds in that order.
In the no-huge configuration the global transparent-huge flags word is zero and the unmapped-area hook is null.
The hugetlb header defines its include guard macro when processed.

Advice, collapse, userfault, NUMA, device-private, split, adjust, and protection-change entry points exist in both configurations but are inert or report failure or success constants when the feature is disabled.
Disabled hugetlb duplication, reservation, sharing, range, zap, reporting, locking, and range-check operations are no-ops or fixed returns, while copy, move, and atomic-fill operations trap and fail.
Disabled hugetlb copy, move, and atomic-fill paths intentionally trap, so they must be unreachable in that configuration.
